claims.claim: Crew Dragon Grace completed the trip from liftoff to docking in seven hours and fifty-five minutes on October 1, 2026.
claims.episode_span: Crew Dragon Grace lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 11:10 a.m. EDT on October 1 and docked to the forward port of the Harmony module at 7:05 p.m. EDT, completing the trip in seven hours and fifty-five minutes.
claims.source_title: Dragon Grace Docks at ISS in 7h55m: US Record [2026]
claims.supporting_quote: SpaceX’s Crew Dragon Grace docked with the International Space Station at 7:05 p.m. EDT (23:05 UTC) on October 1, 2026, just 7 hours and 55 minutes after Crew-13 lifted off from Florida.

claims.claim: The previous US crewed record for launch-to-docking was fourteen hours and forty-three minutes on the Crew-11 mission.
claims.episode_span: The previous US crewed mark stood at fourteen hours and forty-three minutes on the Crew-11 mission.
claims.source_title: Dragon Grace Docks at ISS in 7h55m: US Record [2026]
claims.supporting_quote: The quickest US flight with people on board before Crew-13 had taken 14 hours and 43 minutes, on the Crew-11 mission in August 2025.

claims.claim: Kennedy Space Center construction took five-and-a-half years from groundbreaking to first launch.
claims.episode_span: The analysis places Kennedy Space Center construction at five-and-a-half years from groundbreaking to first launch and Starbase Texas at roughly four-and-a-half years so far.

claims.supporting_quote: NASA built the Kennedy Space Center in about five and a half years, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station took 14 months, and Starbase, Texas, has taken about four and a half years thus far.

claims.claim: Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile urged the FCC to exclude 290 MHz from the proposed satellite spectrum allocation before a Thursday vote.
claims.episode_span: The carriers filed comments urging the commission to exclude the band before a vote scheduled for Thursday. They argue the spectrum should remain reserved for terrestrial 5G rather than shared with non-geostationary satellite systems.
claims.source_title: Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile are trying to shut Starlink out before FCC vote
claims.supporting_quote: ATT, Verizon and T-Mobile want 290 MHz cut from an FCC satellite plan before Thursday.
